recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Revisit only if a future work group decision proposes concrete wording for a specific remaining overlap; broad consolidation of collection resources is not supported by FHIR-14875 or later published clarifications.
issue_request: FHIR-14875 was a Published STU3 FHIR-core/MnM change request resolved Not Persuasive with Modification. It asked to combine collection-like resources such as Composition, Document/Bundle, List, DiagnosticReport, and Questionnaire; the resolution declined consolidation because each resource serves a distinct purpose and said the distinctions belong in the Scope/Boundaries guidance, with more explanation expected around Composition.section, List.entry, and DiagnosticReport.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly applying FHIR-14875 was found; the only git --grep hit for 14875 is an unrelated historical SVN revision number. The principal collection guidance was already present before the issue in d72b1d787a, which added Boundaries and Relationships text for Bundle, Composition, Group, and List. Companion issue FHIR-14729 was resolved Not Persuasive at the same MnM vote because the Boundaries and Relationships sections already documented the differences.
additional_context: MnM minutes from 2018-02-27 confirm the Not Persuasive with Modification vote for FHIR-14875. Later published issues refined the same family of guidance rather than merging resources: FHIR-27083 clarified when Group should be preferred over List, FHIR-27903 added that a List cannot be the subject of an intervention or direct action and updated the List description, and FHIR-19250 clarified DiagnosticReport overlap with DocumentReference. source/fhir.ini confirms the inspected resources are active in the current build.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Current source already distinguishes List, Group, Composition, Bundle, DiagnosticReport, Questionnaire, and related structures in their Scope and Boundaries sections, so adding another general comparison paragraph would be redundant and could drift from the more specific resource-level guidance.
